title: TanStack Query
outcome: Use TanStack Query as the owner of asynchronous server state with deliberate query keys, freshness, invalidation, mutations, and pagination behavior.
artifact: TaskFlow query/mutation layer with stable keys, list/detail caching, invalidation, filters, and debugging via devtools/logs.
labSteps: Install/configure one QueryClient at the correct client boundary.
Define a query-key factory that includes every parameter affecting the result.
Move task-list fetching into query options and observe loading/error/success/cache states.
Add task detail query and prove list/detail caches are distinct.
Implement create/update mutations and choose between invalidation and direct cache updates deliberately.
Add pagination/filter URL state and inspect how query keys prevent cross-filter cache corruption.
failureModes: Random query-key arrays scattered through components
Invalidating too broadly or not at all
mastery: Can explain cache freshness vs garbage collection
principles: TanStack Query owns asynchronous server state; it is not a replacement for every kind of React state.
Choose query keys that uniquely describe the data and parameters being cached.
Invalidate or update the relevant cache after mutations so UI state converges with the server.
Configure stale time and refetch behavior based on data freshness needs rather than copying defaults blindly.
